what: Does the 80% band actually contain the outcome 80% of the time?
method: 20 liquid NSE stocks at 6 point-in-time cut-offs. At each cut-off all later data was removed, volatility estimated from the preceding two years, and 10,000 paths simulated 12 months forward. The resulting 10th-90th percentile band was then compared with the real adjusted close twelve months on.
interpretation: 104 of 120 outcomes landed inside the 80% band — 87%, against the 80% a well-calibrated band should deliver. The 95% interval on that rate is 81-93%. The band is wider than it needs to be, which makes it safe but less informative.
missNarrative: In the most recent window the misses were TCS, HDFCBANK, ITC, TITAN and WIPRO — they moved further than volatility alone implied. The model reads price history. It does not read the future, and it does not see news.
caveats: The six windows overlap, so these forecasts are not independent and the effective sample is smaller than the count.
The universe is large-cap names that still trade today; anything delisted never entered the test, which biases the result upward.
All windows fall in one market regime.
